subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 68-year-old man who lives alone is brought for evaluation of fatigue and leg pain. He has eaten mostly tea and toast for months. Examination shows bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, and poor wound healing, and a blood test confirms vitamin C deficiency.
question: Which of the following steps in collagen synthesis is most directly impaired in this patient?

options.text: Cleavage of the N- and C-terminal propeptides of procollagen
Hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues in the pro-alpha chains
N-linked glycosylation in the endoplasmic reticulum
Cross-linking of collagen molecules by lysyl oxidase
Assembly of collagen fibrils in the extracellular space

explanation_correct: Vitamin C is a required cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase, which hydroxylate proline and lysine residues of the pro-alpha chains; hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine are needed for stable triple helix formation and cross-linking. Deficiency causes scurvy, with bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, and impaired wound healing. Hydroxylation occurs in the RER before glycosylation and triple helix formation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Propeptide cleavage is a proteolytic processing step performed extracellularly and does not require vitamin C.
explanation_incorrect.C: Glycosylation of hydroxylysine residues uses sugars and does not require vitamin C as a cofactor.
explanation_incorrect.D: Lysyl oxidase-mediated cross-linking requires copper, not vitamin C; its deficiency is seen in Menkes disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: Fibril assembly is a later extracellular step and is not directly vitamin C-dependent.

educationalObjective: Vitamin C is required for hydroxylation of proline and lysine during collagen synthesis, and its deficiency causes scurvy.
